title: RAW UNREVIEWED: helioscopium preparation branches grade bowel effect from food to purge
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In Pliny Natural History XXII.29, the helioscopium is boiled as agreeable food, taken with milk as a gentle laxative, and taken as a decoction-potion as an especially strong purgative. Preserve one named source species across preparation/vehicle branches and the stated effect-intensity contrast; do not turn this into an arbitrary plant-use list or extend it to tricoccum.

source.url: retained local complete passage; no external page accessed
source.span: Pliny, Natural History XXII.29, source paragraph 2, AF_COMPLETE_PASSAGE.md; 1856 Bostock/Riley English translation, complete local chapter
source.observed_content: Helioscopium is boiled as agreeable food; taken in milk it is gently laxative; a decoction taken as a potion is a most effectual purgative. The chapter distinguishes helioscopium from tricoccum before these claims.
source.layer: Retained modern English translation of an ancient primary, not a fresh Latin or medieval manuscript collation

potential_admitted_target: None asserted; root must separately nominate and authorize any future complete-unit inspection.

design.mechanism: Keep one named material participant (helioscopium) constant while three source-written operations/vehicles branch: boiling for agreeable food, taking with milk for a mild laxative result, and taking a decoction as a potion for a strong purgative result. The nontrivial constraint is the source's graded effect under distinct preparations, not merely plant-part identity or event order.
design.unit: Complete Pliny XXII.29 chapter, with this design limited to the helioscopium clauses in source paragraph 2; preserve the subsequent paragraph's different tricoccum subject separately.
design.observable_consequence: A future whole-unit reading could only use this model if the same material is retained across separate preparation/vehicle branches and the outcome scale is preserved (culinary food, gentle bowel action, strong purgation). A single undifferentiated prepare/use relation or applying these effects to the second species would fail this source-specific prediction. No target structure or mapping is claimed.
design.scope: Source-only raw hypothesis; unreviewed, unselected, untested, and no target word values

execution_requirements: Root identifies the exact permitted complete unit before any target review; this proposal made no target observation.
Check that one material remains subject of the contrasted preparations and that the source-specific strength contrast is represented rather than supplied by free glosses.
Keep the helioscopium/tricoccum boundary explicit; preserve the rival that these are unrelated catalogue uses rather than an intensity branch.
Treat all efficacy claims as historical assertions, not clinical facts.
assumptions_and_limits: The retained passage is the Bostock/Riley 1856 English translation and not a fresh Latin collation or an independent medieval witness.
The source translation distinguishes helioscopium and tricoccum; modern species identity is disputed in the included editor's notes and is not assigned here.
The phrases 'gently laxative' and 'most effectual purgative' are historical translation claims; no modern pharmacological mechanism is inferred.

IDEA000791 and IDEA000790 concern collection/preservation timing in the same chapter; IDEA000784 concerns carried/knotted plant operations in the tricoccum context. The present branch is preparation-linked graded bowel effect and remains unreviewed for possible source-family overlap.
